questions.stem: A Windows PC shows a Blue Screen of Death (BSOD) with a stop code. What does a BSOD indicate, and what is the primary clue to investigate?

choices.text: A minor application glitch; ignore the on-screen text
A critical stop error, usually bad hardware or a faulty driver; the stop code is the primary clue
A successful Windows update; no action needed
A network outage; check the router

questions.explanation: A BSOD is a critical stop error where the OS shuts down to prevent damage, usually due to bad hardware or a faulty driver. The stop code is your primary clue.
questions.trap: It is not a minor app glitch; the OS halts entirely, and the stop code should be researched, not ignored.

questions.stem: A user reports the computer is running slowly. What is the recommended FIRST tool to investigate resource usage?
questions.explanation: For degraded performance, your first stop is Task Manager - check the Performance tab for spikes and sort the Processes tab to find resource hogs.
questions.trap: Defragmenting blindly does not diagnose what's consuming CPU/memory/disk; Task Manager shows the actual cause first.

questions.stem: A computer displays 'Operating system not found' at boot. What should you check FIRST?

choices.text: Whether a bootable USB drive was left plugged in

questions.explanation: The first thing to check for an 'operating system not found' error is whether a non-bootable USB drive was left plugged in, causing the system to try booting from it.
questions.trap: Replacing the motherboard is a drastic last resort; always check the simple cause (wrong boot device) first.

questions.stem: Windows Startup Repair failed to fix a boot problem. Which recovery-console command manually rebuilds the boot configuration database?
questions.explanation: bootrec /rebuildbcd manually rebuilds the Boot Configuration Database when automatic Startup Repair can't fix the issue.
questions.trap: sfc /scannow repairs system files but does not rebuild the boot configuration database.

questions.stem: An application keeps crashing. Which tool logs every action and error in Windows and is your primary place to investigate?
questions.explanation: Event Viewer logs every action and error in Windows, making it the primary tool for investigating application crashes.
questions.trap: Resource Monitor shows live resource usage but does not keep the historical error log you need to diagnose a crash.

questions.stem: For a more user-friendly view of an application's stability over time, which tool should you check?
questions.explanation: Reliability Monitor tracks an application's stability over time in a user-friendly timeline view.
questions.trap: Disk Management handles partitions and volumes, not application stability history.

questions.stem: A system shows low-memory warnings. Windows uses a paging file on the drive as slow overflow RAM. What is this called, and where do you configure it?

choices.text: Virtual memory; configured in Advanced system settings

questions.explanation: Virtual memory is the paging file on the hard drive that acts as slow overflow RAM; you configure it in Advanced system settings.
questions.trap: ReadyBoost uses a USB drive as cache and is a different feature from the virtual-memory paging file.

questions.stem: A 'USB controller resources exceeded' warning appears. What is the quickest recommended solution?

choices.text: Unplug the device and try a different USB port, which may use a separate controller

questions.explanation: The quickest fix is to unplug the device and try a different USB port, which may connect to a separate controller on the motherboard.
questions.trap: Reinstalling Windows is overkill; the issue is too many complex devices on one controller, solved by moving ports.

questions.stem: A Windows service won't start. According to the review, what should you check first about that service?

choices.text: Whether it has dependencies (other services that must run first) and the correct account permissions
Whether the monitor is plugged in
Whether the keyboard layout is correct
Whether the browser cache is full

questions.explanation: Open the Services app and check whether the service has dependencies (other services that must run first) and verify its account permissions. If it's a Windows service, run sfc; if it's part of an app, reinstall the app.
questions.trap: Monitor, keyboard, and browser cache are unrelated to whether a background service can start.

questions.stem: A computer's clock keeps drifting and becoming inaccurate. What is the simplest fix?

choices.text: Ensure 'set time automatically' is enabled so it syncs with a time server

questions.explanation: Enable 'set time automatically' in the Windows Time & Language settings so the clock syncs with a time server.
questions.trap: Time drift is normal and corrected by syncing with a time server, not by replacing hardware or reinstalling Windows.
